equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A centrally symmetric equilateral polygon is a sum of equal-length segments with freely varying directions. Equiangular polygons instead fix the normal grid and vary segment lengths. Equality in width under these different constraints is not equivalent by a polar or affine transformation: Euclidean side length and Euclidean minimum width are not affine invariants. The odd/even Fourier nullspace classification cannot be inferred from area or support-number stability without an additional proof.

value.rationale: A natural finite-width isoperimetric question gains both a complete restricted extremal answer and an exact, all-side-count classification of nonsmooth infinitesimal stability with a parity-dependent neutral deformation and sharp analytic quadratic loss. The result is a family-level structural boundary relevant to perturbing optimal width, not a routine numerical special case. The broader unrestricted question remains open.
